reference.title: kanamycin nucleotidyltransferase (EC 2.7.7.-), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: Kanamycin nucleotidyltransferase catalyses a single in-line displacement attack by the 4' hydroxyl group of kanamycin on the alpha phosphate of the NTP. The leaving group is pyrophosphate. As is typical for enzymatic phosphodiester reactions, the substitution is concerted with a slightly associative transition-state. a Glu acts as a base to deprotonate the attacking 4' hydroxyl group, while a Lys functions to stabilise the accumulation of negative charge on the alpha phosphate oxygens in the transition state. An Mg2+ ion coordinates the beta and gamma phosphates, so stabilising the departing pyrophosphate leaving group.

reference.title: polynucleotide adenylyltransferase (EC 2.7.7.19), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: From it's crystal structures, Poly(A) polymerase is thought to use the two-metal-ion mechanism proposed for all nucleic acid polymerases. One magnesium ion contacts the 3' OH of the primer and lowers its pKa, activating it for in-line nucleophilic attack on the alpha phosphate of the incoming ATP. Accumulation of negative charge on the alpha phosphate in the pentacoordinate transition state is stabilised by both magnesium ions. The second magnesium ion additionally functions to stabilise accumulation of negative charge on the pyrophosphate leaving group alongside a Lys.

reference.title: PLP-dependent amino-acid decarboxylase (R-CH(NH2)-COOH -> R-CH2-NH2 + CO2)
reference.text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) is bound to an active-site Lys as an internal aldimine. The substrate alpha-amino group displaces the Lys (transaldimination) to form an external aldimine. The bond between C-alpha and the carboxylate, held perpendicular to the pyridine ring, breaks and CO2 leaves; the negative charge is delocalised into the protonated pyridine ring (quinonoid intermediate, PLP acts as an electron sink). Protonation of C-alpha and a second transaldimination by the Lys release the amine product and regenerate the internal aldimine. PLP is not written in the reaction because it is regenerated; CO2 is often omitted from records.

reference.title: L-rhamnose isomerase (EC 5.3.1.14)
reference.text: Isomerization proceeds via a hydride-shift mechanism. In this mechanism, an Asp acts as an acid-base catalyst in ring opening, helping to transfer a proton from O2 to O5. After the ring has been opened, the catalytic water molecule (W4) mediates the transfer of a proton from O1 to O2, and a hydride (H1A), shielded by a Trp from solvent access, attacks C2, producing an aldose with a hydroxyl group (O2) . Steps: (1) an Asp acts as a base via a water molecule to deprotonate  O2 this causes the ring to open. (2) The proton is transferred to O5. (3) an Asp deprotonates O2 via another water molecule. This causes a hydride shift from C2 to C1. (4) The proton is transferred to O1. (5) products.

reference.title: aldose 1-epimerase (EC 5.1.3.3), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: Simultaneous protonation of the oxygen ring by a His and deprotonation of the hydroxyl attached to carbon-1 by a Glu results in ring opening.  Reversal of these protonation events results in ring closure and reversal of configuration about carbon-1. Steps: (1) The carboxylate group of a Glu abstracts the C1 hydroxyl proton and initiates ring opening with concomitant deprotonation of a His. (2) Bond rotation between C1 and C2 is followed by abstraction of the C5 oxygen, and donation of a proton back to the C1 oxygen, forming the product. (3) Products

reference.title: L-fucose isomerase (EC 5.3.1.25)
reference.text: an Asp is thought to act as a general base towards the C1-OH of the cyclic substrate, initiating ring opening. a Glu then abstracts the alpha proton to the aldehyde group, with concomitant deprotonation of an Asp by the developing anion, forming an enol intermediate. an Asp is now charged and acts as a base again but this time at the C2 enol OH, leading to the formation of a ketone group with simultaneous reprotonation of the C1 from a Glu, forming an alpha hydroxyl group. The product cyclises and leaves the active site while a hydroxyl coordinated to the catalytically essential Mn divalent cation deprotonates an Asp, regenerating the active site.

reference.title: ribose-5-phosphate isomerase (EC 5.3.1.6), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text:
The overall mechanism of the reaction is through concerted acid-base catalysis, similar to that employed by Triose Phosphate Isomerase. Initial deprotonation of the C2 atom of Ribose-5-phosphate by the catalytic base a Cys primed by an Asp leads to the formation of an enediolate intermediate. Protons are shuttled via a Thr leaving the C1 oxygen protonated and the C2 oxygen deprotonated. The endiolate then tautomerises forming the product-D-ribulose 5-phosphate. Steps: (1) Isomerization begins with the furanose ring being opened. 
a His accepts a proton from the carbon 1 hydroxyl oxygen and a His donates a proton to the ring oxygen.

reference.title: phosphoribosylanthranilate isomerase (EC 5.3.1.24), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: The general mechanism for this reaction is an Amadori rearrangement. Protonation of the ribosyl ring oxygen by a Cys results in ring opening and formation of an imine intermediate. This intermediate is electrophilic due to the positive charge on the nitrogen, so deprotonation of C2 by an Asp can occur, leading to the formation of the enol tautomer of the product, which rapidly tautomerises to the keto form, the product CdRP. Steps: (1) a Cys acts as a general base in the formation of a Schiff base. It is unkown whether this reaction proceeds through an acid/base catalysed Schiff base mechanism or a "push-pull" proton transfer.

reference.title: 4-hydroxy-2-oxovalerate aldolase (EC 4.1.3.39), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: The proposed catalytic mechanism involves a His acting as a base to remove a proton from the 4-hydroxyl group. Concomitant cleavage of the C3-C4 bond leads to formation of acetaldehyde and the enolate of pyruvate. Accumulation of negative charge on the 2-carbonyl oxygen during formation of the enolate is stabilised by an Mn2+ ion. The enolate is protonated on C3 by a Tyr (which is later re-protonated by a His) to form pyruvate, while the acetaldehyde is passed to the dehydrogenase active site via a tunnel. Access to this tunnel is proposed to be controlled by movements of a Tyr during the catalytic cycle. Steps: (1) a His acts as a base and deprotonates the C4 hydroxyl group.

reference.title: N-acetylneuraminate lyase (EC 4.1.3.3)
reference.text: The initial step is thought to be ring opening of the substrate alpha anomer. The conserved a Lys then acts as nucleophile to the carbonyl group with concomitant proton transfer from a Lys nitrogen to the alcohol group of the tetrahedral intermediate. A second proton transfer results in a cationic oxonium group. The attacking nitrogen lone pair then kicks out a water molecule forming the substrate-enzyme Schiff base intermediate. A tyrosine group mediates the proton abstraction from the hydroxyl at the 4 position by the carboxylate group, leading to the formation of an enamine. Protonation at the methylene carbon then converts the enamine into an imine.

reference.title: tryptophanase (EC 4.1.99.1)
reference.text: The catalytic cycle of tryptophanase consists of the following steps: (1) Association of the amino acid substrate with the enzyme to form the Michaelis complex; (2) Formation of the external aldimine (transaldimination); (3) Quinonoid formation by alpha-proton abstraction from the external aldimine; (4) Tautomerisation of the indolyl group; (5) Elimination of indole and formation of the aminoacrylate Schiff base intermediate; (6) Restoration of the internal aldimine (transaldimination); (7) Release of aminoacrylate and decomposition to pyruvate and ammonia.

reference.title: L-serine ammonia-lyase (EC 4.3.1.17), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: The neutral amine group of L-serine attacks the imine functionality of the pyridoxal-5-phosphate cofactor, forming a Schiff base precursor. The tetrahedral intermediate collapses, generating the external aldimine, PDD-substrate complex. a Lys acts as a general base towards the C-alpha of the covalently bound serine, forming a planar sterocentre [PMID:19640845]. Beta-elimination of water from the carbaion can occur to form an amino-acrylate intermediate. This undergoes non-enzymatic hydrolysis to form water, ammonia and a lysino-alanine modified PLP cofactor which is still capable of isomerase activity [PMID:19155267, PMID:19640845].

No covalent intermediate is formed and the reaction is reversible; the cofactor usually binds first (ordered mechanism).

explanation:
MECHANISM: The Asp residue abstracts a proton from C4 of pregnenolone, deprotonating the C3-OH group, which matches how a base generally initiates reactions of this type. The resulting dienolate intermediate, before the proton is relayed to C6, is stabilized by hydrogen bonds from Tyr and Asp to the C3 oxyanion, as in the reference. The proton is then relayed to C6, via conjugate attack at the catalytic residue, and the resulting enolate isomerizes to form the C4-C5 double bond. This generates the 4,5-epoxysteroid, and subsequently the protonation at C6 by Asp gives the final product, progesterone. NAD+ acts as the electron acceptor, gaining a hydride from C10 and reducing to NADH. The changes in charge on the NAD+ molecule indicate the hydride transfer. log.critique:
## Step 1: Contradictions and unsupported statements:

1. **"The resulting dienolate intermediate, before the proton is relayed to C6, is stabilized by hydrogen bonds from Tyr and Asp to the C3 oxyanion, as in the reference."**  The reference explicitly states that Tyr and Asp stabilize the dienolate intermediate through hydrogen bonding to the C3 **oxyanion**, not the C3 **hydroxyl group**.
2. **"The proton is then relayed to C6, via conjugate attack at the catalytic residue, and the resulting enolate isomerizes to form the C4-C5 double bond."** The reference describes the proton relay to C6 as occurring *before* the enolate isomerization. The enolate isomerization happens *after* the proton is relayed to form the 4,5-epoxysteroid.
3. **"This generates the 4,5-epoxysteroid, and subsequently the protonation at C6 by Asp gives the final product, progesterone."** The reference does not mention the formation of a 4,5-epoxysteroid intermediate. It directly describes the isomerization from a 3-oxo-DELTA5-steroid to a 3-oxo-DELTA4-steroid, which is the final product, progesterone. 
4. **"NAD+ acts as the electron acceptor, gaining a hydride from C10 and reducing to NADH."** While NAD+ does gain a hydride and reduce to NADH, it is not the primary electron acceptor in this reaction. The Asp residue abstracts a proton from C4, which is ultimately transferred to NAD+.

reference.text: Two Mg(II) ions bind to the enzyme. A water bound to Mg(II),  aided by the phosphoryl group of the reactant forms an attacking nucleophilic hydroxide ion to cleave the phosphate-inositolate bond. Subsequent proton transfer steps occur to eliminate the products, myo-inositol and an inorganic phosphate enabling the active site to be ready for another round of catalysis. It has been observed Lithium is a powerful inhibitor of the enzyme due to binding to where one of the magnesium ions usually is found, preventing the phosphate group from leaving. Steps: (1) The phosphoryl oxygen on the myo-inositol phosphate is  protonated by a water molecule.

reference.title: PLP-dependent amino-acid decarboxylase (R-CH(NH2)-COOH -> R-CH2-NH2 + CO2)
reference.text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) is bound to an active-site Lys as an internal aldimine. The substrate alpha-amino group displaces the Lys (transaldimination) to form an external aldimine. The bond between C-alpha and the carboxylate, held perpendicular to the pyridine ring, breaks and CO2 leaves; the negative charge is delocalised into the protonated pyridine ring (quinonoid intermediate, PLP acts as an electron sink). Protonation of C-alpha and a second transaldimination by the Lys release the amine product and regenerate the internal aldimine. PLP is not written in the reaction because it is regenerated; CO2 is often omitted from records.

The obligatory two-electron reduction is shown here to proceed via two direct hydride transfers.

reference.title: dihydroorotase (EC 3.5.2.3)
reference.text: Dihydroorotase uses a bi-nuclear zinc centre to catalyse the reversible formation and hydrolysis of dihydroorotate. In the hydrolysis reaction, the two zinc ions (alpha and beta) coordinate a bridging hydroxide ion that attacks the substrate carbonyl to form a tetrahedral intermediate. This process is facilitated by an Asp acting as a general base to deprotonate the attacking hydroxide, and by polarisation of the carbonyl group through coordination to the beta zinc ion. The tetrahedral intermediate and associated transition state is stabilised by coordination to both zinc ions. Collapse of this intermediate occurs with an Asp acting as a general acid to protate the departing amide nitrogen.

reference.text:
The reaction is initiated by hydride transfer from NADPH to FAD, which in turn transfers electrons, one at a time, to FMN via the 4Fe-4S cluster. The fully reduced FMN provides a hydride ion to the C5 atom of substrate, and Tyr and His are proposed to form a catalytic dyad that protonates the C4 atom of the substrate and completes the reaction. Steps: (1) NADP eliminates a hydride ion, which is added to FAD. 
The nicotinamide ring of NADP interacts with the re-face of the isoalloxazine ring, resulting in fully reduced FAD [PMID:12840019]. (2) FAD transfers a single electron, through a Gln and an iron-sulfur cluster, to FMN, which deprotonates water.

reference.title: PLP-dependent amino-acid decarboxylase (R-CH(NH2)-COOH -> R-CH2-NH2 + CO2)
reference.text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) is bound to an active-site Lys as an internal aldimine. The substrate alpha-amino group displaces the Lys (transaldimination) to form an external aldimine. The bond between C-alpha and the carboxylate, held perpendicular to the pyridine ring, breaks and CO2 leaves; the negative charge is delocalised into the protonated pyridine ring (quinonoid intermediate, PLP acts as an electron sink). Protonation of C-alpha and a second transaldimination by the Lys release the amine product and regenerate the internal aldimine. PLP is not written in the reaction because it is regenerated; CO2 is often omitted from records.

reference.text: Two Mg(II) ions bind to the enzyme. It has been observed Lithium is a powerful inhibitor of the enzyme due to binding to where one of the magnesium ions usually is found, preventing the phosphate group from leaving. reference.text: As with most phosphatases the mechanism involves nucleophilic attack on the phosphate group. The nucleophile is an activated water molecule, which is co-ordinated to two magnesium cofactors and then activated by a Thr. This attacks the phosphate group forming a trigonal bipyramidal intermediate which is stabilised by the magnesium ions, break down of this leads to the the inositol 4-phosphate. Steps: (1) The an Asp/a Thr network deprotonates a water molecule activating it for nucleophilic attack on the phosphate. The penta-covalent intermediate formed is stabilized by the magnesium ions. (2) The intermediate collapses yielding inositol 4-phosphate.

reference.title: Cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (heme-thiolate; R-H + O2 + 2e- -> R-OH + H2O)
reference.text: P450s carry a heme iron ligated by a Cys thiolate. The two electrons come from NADPH via NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, a FAD/FMN flavoprotein (written in some databases as '[reduced NADPH-hemoprotein reductase]', and in some reaction records as FMNH2 or NADPH). Cycle: substrate binds, Fe3+ is reduced to Fe2+, O2 binds, a second electron and two protons cleave the O-O bond releasing water and forming Compound I (Fe(IV)=O porphyrin radical cation). For aliphatic C-H hydroxylation Compound I abstracts a hydrogen atom and the carbon radical recombines with the Fe-OH ('oxygen rebound').

reference.text:
It has been propose that a movement of FAD takes place in concert with a large conformational change of residues 170-210 during catalysis. The catalytic mechanism of PHHY is complex, involving FAD and three substrates: molecular oxygen, phenol and NADPH. The overall mechanism is of the type bi-uni-uni-bi ping pong. While in the past the mechanism has been compared to p-hydroxy-benzoate hydroxylase, the enzymes are now though to operate differently.

reference.title: 5'-nucleotidase (bacterial) (EC 3.1.3.5), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: 5'-nucleotidase catalyses the hydrolytic cleavage of 5'-mononucleotides to nucleoside and phosphate by nucleophilic attack of a water molecule on the phosphorous. A water ligand is coordinated to the di-zinc centre. The phosphate group of the substrate binds with one oxygen atom to a metal ion. The metal-bound water attacks the phosphorous nucleophilically, with the proton transferred to a His. The pentahedral transition state is stabilised by both metal ions, an Asn, an Arg, an Arg, an Arg and a His. After expulsion of the leaving group the tetrahedral phosphate ion remains bound to the dimetal centre.

reference.title: inositol-phosphate phosphatase (EC 3.1.3.25), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: Two Mg(II) ions bind to the enzyme. A water bound to Mg(II),  aided by the phosphoryl group of the reactant forms an attacking nucleophilic hydroxide ion to cleave the phosphate-inositolate bond. Subsequent proton transfer steps occur to eliminate the products, myo-inositol and an inorganic phosphate enabling the active site to be ready for another round of catalysis. It has been observed Lithium is a powerful inhibitor of the enzyme due to binding to where one of the magnesium ions usually is found, preventing the phosphate group from leaving. Steps: (1) The phosphoryl oxygen on the myo-inositol phosphate is  protonated by a water molecule.

reference.title: inositol-1,4-bisphosphate 1-phosphatase (EC 3.1.3.57), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: As with most phosphatases the mechanism involves nucleophilic attack on the phosphate group. The nucleophile is an activated water molecule, which is co-ordinated to two magnesium cofactors and then activated by a Thr. This attacks the phosphate group forming a trigonal bipyramidal intermediate which is stabilised by the magnesium ions, break down of this leads to the the inositol 4-phosphate. Steps: (1) The an Asp/a Thr network deprotonates a water molecule activating it for nucleophilic attack on the phosphate. The penta-covalent intermediate formed is stabilized by the magnesium ions. (2) The intermediate collapses yielding inositol 4-phosphate.

reference.title: dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (NADP+) (EC 1.3.1.2), an enzyme of the same sub-subclass
reference.text: The enzyme uses electrons from NADPH to reduce the uracil substrate. However, the electrons are not passed directly to uracil but instead are transferred from NADPH to FAD and then from FAD to FMN. Finally the FMN acts as a nucleophile to transfer a hydride ion to the double bond of the uracil. This creates a transient carbanion at the second carbon of the double bond, allowing protonation by a Cys to occur, completing the reaction. Steps: (1) Binding of NADPH results in a conformational change which facilitates the transfer of a hydride from its pro-S position to the re-face of FAD at N5. Following this step two single electron transfers then occur via the FeS clusters to FMN.

reference.title: Acyl-CoA:alcohol O-acyltransferase (acyl-CoA + R-OH -> ester + CoA)
reference.text: The acceptor hydroxyl group attacks the thioester carbonyl carbon of the acyl-CoA. A conserved active-site His (e.g. in DGAT1 and other MBOAT-family acyltransferases, and in DGAT2/LPAAT-type enzymes) acts as general base, deprotonating the hydroxyl. The tetrahedral oxyanion intermediate collapses, expelling the CoA thiolate (protonated to CoA-SH) and forming the ester bond. The acyl group is transferred directly from CoA to the acceptor; CoA is the leaving group and is usually omitted from records.

reference.title: PLP-dependent amino-acid decarboxylase (R-CH(NH2)-COOH -> R-CH2-NH2 + CO2)
reference.text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) is bound to an active-site Lys as an internal aldimine. The substrate alpha-amino group displaces the Lys (transaldimination) to form an external aldimine. The bond between C-alpha and the carboxylate, held perpendicular to the pyridine ring, breaks and CO2 leaves; the negative charge is delocalised into the protonated pyridine ring (quinonoid intermediate, PLP acts as an electron sink). Protonation of C-alpha and a second transaldimination by the Lys release the amine product and regenerate the internal aldimine. PLP is not written in the reaction because it is regenerated; CO2 is often omitted from records.

The bond between C-alpha and the carboxylate, held perpendicular to the pyridine ring, breaks and CO2 leaves; the negative charge is delocalised into the protonated pyridine ring (quinonoid intermediate, PLP acts as an electron sink). Protonation of C-alpha and a second transaldimination by the Lys release the amine product and regenerate the internal aldimine. PLP is not written in the reaction because it is regenerated; CO2 is often omitted from records.

reference.title: CDP-alcohol phosphotransferase (CDP-X + R-OH -> R-O-P(O2)-O-X + CMP)
reference.text: CDP-alcohol phosphotransferases (CDP-AP family: ethanolamine/choline phosphotransferases, phosphatidylinositol/-serine/-glycerophosphate synthases, eukaryotic cardiolipin synthase) are membrane enzymes with a conserved Asp-rich motif (D-G-x2-A-R-x8-G-x3-D-x3-D) that binds Mg2+ ions. A conserved Asp acts as general base and deprotonates the acceptor hydroxyl, which attacks the phosphorus atom that is NOT attached to the cytidine nucleoside (the distal phosphate of CDP-X) in an in-line SN2-type substitution; the Mg2+ ions neutralise the diphosphate and stabilise the leaving group, CMP. The product is a new phosphodiester linking the acceptor to the X group; CMP is usually omitted from records.

reference.title: Acyl-CoA:alcohol O-acyltransferase (acyl-CoA + R-OH -> ester + CoA)
reference.text: The acceptor hydroxyl group attacks the thioester carbonyl carbon of the acyl-CoA. A conserved active-site His (e.g. in DGAT1 and other MBOAT-family acyltransferases, and in DGAT2/LPAAT-type enzymes) acts as general base, deprotonating the hydroxyl. The tetrahedral oxyanion intermediate collapses, expelling the CoA thiolate (protonated to CoA-SH) and forming the ester bond. The acyl group is transferred directly from CoA to the acceptor; CoA is the leaving group and is usually omitted from records.

reference.title: dihydroorotase (EC 3.5.2.3)
reference.text: Dihydroorotase uses a bi-nuclear zinc centre to catalyse the reversible formation and hydrolysis of dihydroorotate. In the hydrolysis reaction, the two zinc ions (alpha and beta) coordinate a bridging hydroxide ion that attacks the substrate carbonyl to form a tetrahedral intermediate. This process is facilitated by an Asp acting as a general base to deprotonate the attacking hydroxide, and by polarisation of the carbonyl group through coordination to the beta zinc ion. The tetrahedral intermediate and associated transition state is stabilised by coordination to both zinc ions. Collapse of this intermediate occurs with an Asp acting as a general acid to protate the departing amide nitrogen.

reference.title: phosphomannomutase/ phosphoglucomutase (EC 5.4.2.8)
reference.text: Residues an Arg, a His, a Lys, an Arg and a His along with cofactor Mg(II) form a positive electrostatic field. The substrate O atom then nucleophilically attacks the phosphorus of Sep 108, which acts as an electrophile, and the Serine O-P bond is broken. The above residues (and co-factor) then act to stabilise a Ser alkoxide. Rotation of the substrate occurs, arranging the C6 phospho group toward a Ser. a Ser then nucleophilically attacks the C6 phosphorus atom, breaking the P-O bond of the substrate. The substrate is then re-protonated to form the 1-P product.

reference.text: CDP-alcohol phosphotransferases (CDP-AP family: ethanolamine/choline phosphotransferases, phosphatidylinositol/-serine/-glycerophosphate synthases, eukaryotic cardiolipin synthase) are membrane enzymes with a conserved Asp-rich motif (D-G-x2-A-R-x8-G-x3-D-x3-D) that binds Mg2+ ions.
